passages.text: “I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them important things.
He wanted to help them.
He did not want them to fall away.
He gave them these words to keep them strong.
passages.original: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ σκανδαλισθῆτε

passages.text: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about the future.
People will put you out of the synagogues.
A time will come.
At that time, someone may kill you.
That person will think he is serving God by doing this.
passages.original: ἀποσυναγώγους ποιήσουσιν ὑμᾶς ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα ἵνα πᾶς ὁ ἀποκτείνας ὑμᾶς δόξῃ λατρείαν προσφέρειν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or Me.
passages.sermon: They will do these things.\r\nThey have not known the Father.\r\nThey have not known Me.
passages.original: καὶ ταῦτα ποιήσουσιν ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸν Πατέρα οὐδὲ ἐμέ

passages.text: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them what would happen in the future.
He wanted them to remember His words when these things happened.
He said, “I have told you these things so you will remember I warned you.”
He did not tell them these things at first.
He was with them from the beginning.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἡ ὥρα αὐτῶν μνημονεύητε αὐτῶν ὅτι ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν ταῦτα δὲ ὑμῖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς οὐκ εἶπον ὅτι μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἤμην

passages.text: Now, however, I am going to Him who sent Me; yet none of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said He is going to the One who sent Him.
God the Father sent Jesus.
Jesus is now returning to the Father.
None of the disciples ask Jesus, “Where are you going?”
passages.original: Νῦν δὲ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐρωτᾷ με Ποῦ ὑπάγεις

passages.text: Instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe told them important things.\r\nBecause He spoke these things, their hearts became full of sorrow.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὅτι ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἡ λύπη πεπλήρωκεν ὑμῶν τὴν καρδίαν

passages.text: But I tell you the truth, it is for your benefit that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus always told the truth.
Jesus said, "It is good for you that I am going away."
If I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you.
If I go, I will send the Advocate to you.
The Advocate is the Holy Spirit.
God will send the Holy Spirit to help you after I leave.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω ὑμῖν συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐγὼ ἀπέλθω ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ ἀπέλθω ὁ Παράκλητος οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐὰν δὲ πορευθῶ πέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And when He comes, He will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment: in regard to sin, because they do not believe in Me; in regard to righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see Me; and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned.
passages.sermon:
The Advocate is the Holy Spirit.
The Holy Spirit will come.
When He comes, He will convict the world.
He will convict the world about sin.
He will convict the world about righteousness.
He will convict the world about judgment.
He will convict the world about sin because people do not believe in Jesus.
He will convict the world about righteousness because Jesus is going to the Father.
You will not see Jesus anymore because He is going to the Father.
He will convict the world about judgment because the ruler of this world has been condemned.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐκεῖνος ἐλέγξει τὸν κόσμον περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ περὶ κρίσεως περὶ ἁμαρτίας μέν ὅτι οὐ πιστεύουσιν εἰς ἐμέ περὶ δικαιοσύνης δέ ὅτι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα ὑπάγω καὶ οὐκέτι θεωρεῖτέ με περὶ δὲ κρίσεως ὅτι ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου κέκριται

passages.text: I still have much to tell you, but you cannot yet bear to hear it.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus had many more things to tell them.\r\nThe disciples could not bear to hear these things yet.
passages.original: Ἔτι πολλὰ ἔχω ὑμῖν λέγειν ἀλλ’ οὐ δύνασθε βαστάζειν ἄρτι

passages.text: However, when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit of truth will come.
The Spirit of truth will guide you.
He will guide you into all truth.
The Spirit will not speak on His own.
He will speak what He hears.
He will declare to you what is to come.
passages.original: ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πάσῃ οὐ γὰρ λαλήσει ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ἀλλ’ ὅσα ἀκούσει λαλήσει καὶ τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν

passages.text: He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.
passages.sermon: The Spirit of truth will glorify Me.\r\nHe will take what belongs to Me.\r\nHe will reveal it to you.
passages.original: ἐκεῖνος ἐμὲ δοξάσει ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λήμψεται καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν

passages.text: Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus says, “Everything the Father has belongs to Me.”
The Father is God.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus says, “This is why I told you that the Spirit will take from what is Mine.”
The Spirit is the Spirit of truth.
The Spirit will reveal to you what belongs to Me.”
passages.original: πάντα ὅσα ἔχει ὁ Πατὴρ ἐμά ἐστιν διὰ τοῦτο εἶπον ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ λαμβάνει καὶ ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν

passages.text: In a little while you will see Me no more, and then after a little while you will see Me.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “In a little while, you will not see Me.\r\nThen, after a little while, you will see Me again.”
passages.original: Μικρὸν καὶ οὐκέτι θεωρεῖτέ με καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με

passages.text: Then some of His disciples asked one another, “Why is He telling us, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’ and ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
passages.sermon:
Some of Jesus’ disciples spoke to each other.
They asked a question.
They said, “Why is Jesus telling us this?”
They repeated Jesus’ words.
He said, ‘In a little while you will not see Me.’
He also said, ‘After a little while you will see Me.’
He said, ‘Because I am going to the Father.’
The disciples wanted to know what Jesus meant.
passages.original: Εἶπαν οὖν ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς ἀλλήλους Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο ὃ λέγει ἡμῖν Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με καί Ὅτι ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα

passages.text: They kept asking, “Why is He saying, ‘a little while’? We do not understand what He is saying.”
passages.sermon:
Some of Jesus’ disciples spoke together.
They talked about Jesus’ words.
They said, “Why is He saying, ‘a little while’?”
They did not understand Jesus’ meaning.
They said, “We do not know what He is saying.”
passages.original: ἔλεγον οὖν Τοῦτο τί ἐστιν ὃ λέγει Τὸ μικρόν οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί λαλεῖ

passages.text: Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them, “Are you asking one another why I said, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the teacher.
Jesus knew His disciples wanted to ask Him a question.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "You are asking each other about what I said."
Jesus said, "I told you, 'In a little while you will not see Me.'"
Jesus said, "Then after a little while you will see Me again."
passages.original: Ἔγνω ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤθελον αὐτὸν ἐρωτᾶν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Περὶ τούτου ζητεῖτε μετ’ ἀλλήλων ὅτι εἶπον Μικρὸν καὶ οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με καὶ πάλιν μικρὸν καὶ ὄψεσθέ με

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
You will weep.
You will wail.
The world will rejoice.
You will feel sorrow.
But your sorrow will become joy.”
passages.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι κλαύσετε καὶ θρηνήσετε ὑμεῖς ὁ δὲ κόσμος χαρήσεται ὑμεῖς λυπηθήσεσθε ἀλλ’ ἡ λύπη ὑμῶν εἰς χαρὰν γενήσεται

passages.text: A woman has pain in childbirth because her time has come; but when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
passages.sermon:
A woman feels pain when she gives birth.
Her pain comes because her time to give birth has arrived.
After she gives birth to the child, she does not remember her suffering.
She forgets her pain because she feels great joy.
She is joyful because a child has been born into the world.
passages.original: ἡ γυνὴ ὅταν τίκτῃ λύπην ἔχει ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα αὐτῆς ὅταν δὲ γεννήσῃ τὸ παιδίον οὐκέτι μνημονεύει τῆς θλίψεως διὰ τὴν χαρὰν ὅτι ἐγεννήθη ἄνθρωπος εἰς τὸν κόσμον

passages.text: So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
passages.sermon:
You have sorrow now.
I will see you again.
Your hearts will rejoice.
No one will take away your joy.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς οὖν νῦν μὲν λύπην ἔχετε πάλιν δὲ ὄψομαι ὑμᾶς καὶ χαρήσεται ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία καὶ τὴν χαρὰν ὑμῶν οὐδεὶς αἴρει ἀφ’ ὑμῶν

passages.text: In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “In that day, you will not ask Me anything.
I tell you the truth.
If you ask the Father for anything in My name, He will give it to you.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἐρωτήσετε οὐδέν ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἄν τι αἰτήσητε τὸν Πατέρα δώσει ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου

passages.text: Until now you have not asked for anything in My name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said they had not asked for anything in His name until now.
He told them to ask in His name.
He promised they would receive what they asked.
He said this would make their joy complete.
passages.original: ἕως ἄρτι οὐκ ᾐτήσατε οὐδὲν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου αἰτεῖτε καὶ λήμψεσθε ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ὑμῶν ᾖ πεπληρωμένη

passages.text: I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus has used figures of speech to teach them.
He has not always spoken plainly.
A time will come soon.
In that time, Jesus will not use figures of speech.
He will speak clearly to them.
He will tell them plainly about the Father.
passages.original: Ταῦτα ἐν παροιμίαις λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὐκέτι ἐν παροιμίαις λαλήσω ὑμῖν ἀλλὰ παρρησίᾳ περὶ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν

passages.text: In that day you will ask in My name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them about a future day.
On that day, they would ask in His name.
Jesus said He would not need to ask the Father for them.
They would ask the Father themselves in Jesus’ name.
passages.original: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου αἰτήσεσθε καὶ οὐ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐρωτήσω τὸν Πατέρα περὶ ὑμῶν

passages.text: For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.
passages.sermon:
The Father Himself loves you.
You have loved Me.
You have believed that I came from God.
Because of this, the Father loves you.
passages.original: αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ φιλεῖ ὑμᾶς ὅτι ὑμεῖς ἐμὲ πεφιλήκατε καὶ πεπιστεύκατε ὅτι ἐγὼ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον

passages.text: I came from the Father and entered the world. In turn, I will leave the world and go to the Father.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus came from the Father.
Jesus entered the world.
Jesus will leave the world.
Jesus will go to the Father.
passages.original: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ ἐλήλυθα εἰς τὸν κόσμον πάλιν ἀφίημι τὸν κόσμον καὶ πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα

passages.text: His disciples said, “See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had disciples.
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Now you are speaking plainly.
You are not using any figures of speech.”
passages.original: Λέγουσιν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Ἴδε νῦν ἐν παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖς καὶ παροιμίαν οὐδεμίαν λέγεις

passages.text: Now we understand that You know all things and that You have no need for anyone to question You. Because of this, we believe that You came from God.”
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Now we understand something about You.
You know all things.
You do not need anyone to ask You questions.
Because of this, we believe something important.
We believe that You came from God.”
passages.original: νῦν οἴδαμεν ὅτι οἶδας πάντα καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχεις ἵνα τίς σε ἐρωτᾷ ἐν τούτῳ πιστεύομεν ὅτι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθες

passages.text: “Do you finally believe?” Jesus replied.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus asked them a question.\r\nJesus said, “Do you now believe?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς Ἄρτι πιστεύετε

passages.text: “Look, an hour is coming and has already come when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about what would happen soon.
He said, “Look, the hour is coming.
In fact, it has already come.
You will be scattered.
Each of you will go to your own home.
You will leave Me alone.
But I am not alone.
The Father is with Me.”
passages.original: ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ ἐλήλυθεν ἵνα σκορπισθῆτε ἕκαστος εἰς τὰ ἴδια κἀμὲ μόνον ἀφῆτε καὶ οὐκ εἰμὶ μόνος ὅτι ὁ Πατὴρ μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν

passages.text: I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus wanted them to understand something important.
He said, “I have told you these things.”
He wanted them to have peace in Him.
He said, “In Me you may have peace.”
He explained the reality of the world.
He said, “In the world you will have trouble.”
He encouraged them to be brave.
He said, “Take courage.”
He declared His victory.
He said, “I have overcome the world.”
passages.original: ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ εἰρήνην ἔχητε ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλῖψιν ἔχετε ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον
